==Music==
{{Main|Gladiator II (soundtrack)}}
[[Harry Gregson-Williams]] composed the score for the film, taking over from [[Hans Zimmer]] and [[Lisa Gerrard]] who had scored the first film.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ritman |first1=Alex |title=Ridley Scott's 'Gladiator 2' Taps Hans Zimmer Protégé Harry Gregson-Williams as Composer (EXCLUSIVE) |url=https://variety.com/2024/film/news/gladiator-2-ridley-scott-composer-harry-gregson-williams-hans-zimmer-1235862580/ |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |access-date=January 5, 2024 |date=January 5, 2024 |archive-date=January 5, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240105161558/https://variety.com/2024/film/news/gladiator-2-ridley-scott-composer-harry-gregson-williams-hans-zimmer-1235862580/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Zimmer decided not to return because he did not want to repeat his work from the first film. In an interview with [[Curzon Cinemas|Curzon]], he said that the film was "in really good hands" with Gregson-Williams, who had started his career as Zimmer's assistant.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Warmann |first1=Amon |url=https://www.curzon.com/journal/hans-zimmer-interview/ |title=HANS ZIMMER: 'I HAD TO CHANGE STYLE BECAUSE EVERYONE ELSE WAS DOING MINE' |website=[[Curzon Cinemas|Curzon]] |date=March 6, 2024 |access-date=June 15, 2024 |archive-date=June 15, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240615063632/https://www.curzon.com/journal/hans-zimmer-interview/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Gregson-Williams wrote 100 minutes of original score for the film, and used some of Zimmer and Gerrard's musical cues from the first film.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2024/11/gladiator-ii-composer-harry-gregson-williams-interview-sound-and-screen-1236165215/ |title='Gladiator II' Composer Harry Gregson-Williams Sought Mentor Hans Zimmer's Approval To Tackle Sequel & Borrow Cues From The First Film – Sound & Screen Film |website= Deadline |date=November 2, 2024 |access-date=November 2, 2024}}</ref>

==Release==
===Theatrical===
''Gladiator II'' had its world premiere in [[Sydney]] on October 30, 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://au.lifestyle.yahoo.com/paul-mescal-stunned-by-detail-at-gladiator-ii-sydney-premiere-absolutely-mad-235858167.html|title=Paul Mescal stunned by detail at Gladiator II Sydney premiere: 'Absolutely mad'|first=Marni|last=Dixit|website=[[Yahoo|Yahoo! Lifestyle]]|date=October 31, 2024|access-date=November 12, 2024}}</ref> It was released more widely in Australia, Italy and New Zealand on November 14.<ref>{{cite web|last=Choy|first=Rachel|url=https://www.pedestrian.tv/entertainment/gladiator-ii-release-date-trailer-plot-cast-paul-mescal/|title=Gladiator II: Everything We Know Including Trailer, Plot, Release Date & Cast|date=July 10, 2024|website=[[Pedestrian.tv]]|publisher=[[Nine Entertainment Co.]]|access-date=August 12, 2024|archive-date=August 12, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812035321/https://www.pedestrian.tv/entertainment/gladiator-ii-release-date-trailer-plot-cast-paul-mescal/|url-status=live}}</ref> It was released in the United Kingdom and some other territories the following day, and in the United States and Canada on November 22. [[Universal Pictures]] declined to co-finance the sequel or distribute it overseas as it had the first film, leaving only [[Paramount Pictures]] as the worldwide distributor.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://collider.com/gladiator-2-release-date-change/ |title='Gladiator 2' Just Won the Battle for an Earlier Release Date Internationally |website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |last=McPherson |first=Chris |date=June 19, 2024 |access-date=June 21, 2024 |archive-date=June 19, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240619235812/https://collider.com/gladiator-2-release-date-change/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="TartaglioneDeadline">{{Cite web |last=Tartaglione |first=Nancy |date=June 19, 2024 |title=Paramount Goes Epic At CineEurope With 'Gladiator II' Footage; Highlights 'A Quiet Place: Day One' & 'Transformers One' |url=https://deadline.com/2024/06/paramount-gladiator-2-a-quiet-place-day-one-transformers-cineeurope-1235977955/ |access-date=June 29, 2024 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |language=en-US |archive-date=June 20, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240620011308/https://deadline.com/2024/06/paramount-gladiator-2-a-quiet-place-day-one-transformers-cineeurope-1235977955/ |url-status=live }}</ref> It was previously scheduled for a global release on November 22.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2023/02/gladiator-2-release-date-1235249039/ |title='Gladiator 2′ Gets Pre-Thanksgiving 2024 Release |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony |date=February 3, 2023 |access-date=February 3, 2023 |archive-date=July 5, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230705122650/https://deadline.com/2023/02/gladiator-2-release-date-1235249039/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

On July 1, 2024, it had been announced that the film's release date would be shared with [[Wicked (2024 film)|''Wicked'']], whose date was moved from November 27 to avoid competition with ''[[Moana 2]]''. This sparked speculation on whether pitting the two films together could lead to a scenario similar to the [[Barbenheimer]] phenomenon, which was a result of ''[[Barbie (film)|Barbie]]'' and ''[[Oppenheimer (film)|Oppenheimer]]'' both being released on July 21, 2023.<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Blistein |first1=Jon |date=July 2, 2024 |title=If 'Wicked' and 'Gladiator 2' Is the Next 'Barbenheimer,' It Needs a Better Portmanteau Than 'Wickiator' |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-news/wicked-gladiator-2-same-release-date-barbenheimer-1235051572/ |access-date=July 5, 2024 |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |archive-date=July 3, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240703101340/https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-news/wicked-gladiator-2-same-release-date-barbenheimer-1235051572/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On July 10, 2024, Mescal called the double release "Glicked" and voiced his support for the two films to be shown as a [[double feature]], saying "It would be amazing 'cause I think the films couldn't be more polar opposites and it worked in that context previously. So, fingers crossed people come out and see both films on opening weekend".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bergeson |first1=Samantha |title=Paul Mescal Anoints the Next 'Barbenheimer' with 'Gladiator 2' and 'Wicked' Opening Same Day: 'Glicked' |url=https://www.indiewire.com/news/general-news/paul-mescal-gladiator-2-wicked-double-feature-glicked-1235024053/ |website=IndieWire |access-date=July 10, 2024 |date=July 10, 2024 |archive-date=July 16, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240716020555/https://www.indiewire.com/news/general-news/paul-mescal-gladiator-2-wicked-double-feature-glicked-1235024053/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Home media===
''Gladiator II'' was released on [[Digital distribution|digital download]] on December 24, 2024,<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lammer |first1=Tim |title='Gladiator II' Gets Digital Streaming Premiere Date |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/timlammers/2024/12/14/gladiator-ii-gets-digital-streaming-premiere-date/ |website=[[Forbes]] |access-date=December 14, 2024 |date=December 14, 2024 |archive-date=December 15, 2024 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241215010728/https://www.forbes.com/sites/timlammers/2024/12/14/gladiator-ii-gets-digital-streaming-premiere-date/ |url-status=live}}</ref> and on [[Ultra HD Blu-ray]] and [[Blu-ray Disc]] on March 4, 2025.<ref>{{cite web |title=Gladiator II 4K Blu-ray |url=https://www.blu-ray.com/news/?id=35708 |website=Blu-ray.com |access-date=January 21, 2025 |date=December 23, 2024}}</ref>

===Rating===
Much like the original film, ''Gladiator II'' was [[R rating (Motion Picture Association)|rated R]] by the [[Motion Picture Association]] due to "strong bloody violence".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rigdely |first=Charlie |title=Gladiator II Rating Confirms the Colosseum Will Get Bloody |url=https://comicbook.com/movies/news/gladiator-2-movie-rating-r-ridley-scott-colosseum/ |website=[[ComicBook.com]] |access-date=August 28, 2024 |date=August 27, 2024 |archive-date=August 28, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240828132451/https://comicbook.com/movies/news/gladiator-2-movie-rating-r-ridley-scott-colosseum/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Unlike other past films of his, Scott stated that ''Gladiator II'' will not receive a [[director's cut]], as he earned the right to have [[Final cut privilege|final cut]] and removed some scenes during filming so he did not need to do so after finishing the film.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Jones |first1=Tamera |last2=Weintraub |first2=Steven |url=https://collider.com/ridley-scott-gladiator-2-stanley-kubric-2001-space-odyssey/ |title="It Warns Us What Happens If We Allow AI Into Our Universe": Ridley Scott Explains How '2001 A Space Odyssey' Predetermined The Future |access-date=November 5, 2024 |date=November 3, 2024 |website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] }}</ref>

In Australia, two cuts of the film were released; the original, uncut [[Australian Classification Board|MA15+]] version (with the consumer advice "strong [[Thematic elements|themes]] and violence"),<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.classification.gov.au/titles/gladiator-ii-1|title=Gladiator II |date=November 21, 2024 |website=[[Australian Classification Board]] |access-date=November 28, 2024}}{{dead link|date=May 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> and the edited M-rated version ("[[animal cruelty]], blood and gore, injury detail and violence") where blood spray is either trimmed down or removed.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Van Reeth |first=Magali |url=https://www.signis.world/news/media/film-reviews/15-11-2024/gladiator-ii-by-ridley-scott/ |title=GLADIATOR II by Ridley Scott |date=November 15, 2024 |website=[[SIGNIS]] |access-date=November 25, 2024 |archive-date=November 18, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241118095202/https://www.signis.world/news/media/film-reviews/15-11-2024/gladiator-ii-by-ridley-scott/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The MA15+ rating was reinstated for the uncut home media release, with a revised consumer advice of "[[Thematic elements|strong animal cruelty]], violence and blood and gore".<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.classification.gov.au/titles/gladiator-ii-home-entertainment-version|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241209223222/https://www.classification.gov.au/titles/gladiator-ii-home-entertainment-version|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 9, 2024|title=Gladiator II (Home Entertainment Version)|date=November 25, 2024 |website=[[Australian Classification Board]] |access-date=December 10, 2024}}</ref>

===Marketing===
Footage of the film screened at the [[National Association of Theatre Owners#CinemaCon|CinemaCon]] 2024 in [[Las Vegas]] included scenes of Joseph Quinn as Geta dressed in a white toga and laurel-leaf crown dramatically plunging his thumb downward to note the fate of defeated gladiators, with Nielsen in the background.<ref name="QuinnEW" /> In June of that year, Scott showcased an extended clip of the film featuring Denzel Washington, Paul Mescal, Pedro Pascal, Connie Nielsen, and Quinn.<ref name="TartaglioneDeadline"/>

A poster for the film was released on July 8, 2024, with a trailer released the following day.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Adams |first1=Timothy |title=First Gladiator 2 Poster Released Ahead of Trailer Debut |url=https://comicbook.com/movies/news/gladiator-2-first-poster-trailer-release-date/ |website=[[ComicBook.com]] |date=July 8, 2024 |access-date=July 8, 2024 |language=en |archive-date=July 8, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240708180620/https://comicbook.com/movies/news/gladiator-2-first-poster-trailer-release-date/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The trailer would also reportedly be attached to the [[Marvel Cinematic Universe]] (MCU) film ''[[Deadpool & Wolverine]]'', which was released on July 26, 2024.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://collider.com/gladiator-2-trailer-release/ |title=Here's When the 'Gladiator 2' Trailer Will Drop [Exclusive] |website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |last=McPherson |first=Chris |date=June 24, 2024 |access-date=June 25, 2024 |archive-date=June 25, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240625005645/https://collider.com/gladiator-2-trailer-release/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Jennifer Ouellette of ''[[Ars Technica]]'' said the trailer indicated the film "promises to be just as much of a visual feast, as a new crop of power players (plus a couple of familiar faces) clash over the future of Rome".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ouellette |first=Jennifer |date=July 9, 2024 |title=It's another bloody power struggle for Rome's future in Gladiator II trailer |url=https://arstechnica.com/culture/2024/07/its-another-bloody-power-struggle-for-romes-future-in-gladiator-ii-trailer/ |access-date=July 10, 2024 |website=[[Ars Technica]] |language=en-us |archive-date=July 10, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240710000900/https://arstechnica.com/culture/2024/07/its-another-bloody-power-struggle-for-romes-future-in-gladiator-ii-trailer/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Rather than using an orchestral score, the first trailer used "[[No Church in the Wild]]" by [[Jay-Z]] and [[Kanye West]], which caused a backlash among film fans who said it was too modern of a song choice. Some justified this choice of music by citing the trailer for the first ''Gladiator'' which had used "[[Bawitdaba]]" by [[Kid Rock]].<ref>{{cite news | date = July 10, 2024 | url = https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/news/gladiator-2-trailer-no-church-in-the-wild-song-b2577211.html | access-date = July 13, 2024 | newspaper = The Independent | title = Gladiator 2 trailer causes ridiculous debate among film fans | first = Jacob | last = Stolworthy | archive-date = July 12, 2024 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20240712134936/https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/news/gladiator-2-trailer-no-church-in-the-wild-song-b2577211.html | url-status = live }}</ref> ''[[Screen Rant]]'' criticized how the second trailer [[Spoiler (media)|spoiled]] the [[plot twist]] of Maximus being Lucius' father; while a common fan theory since the first film's release, Adam Bentz found it questionable to reveal in a trailer, as it could have been emotionally impactful for audiences like it was for Mescal when he found out his character's relationship with the original's protagonist.<ref>{{cite news | date = October 22, 2024 | url = https://screenrant.com/gladiator-2-maximus-father-twist-paul-mescal-response/ | access-date = October 23, 2024 | newspaper = [[Screen Rant]] | title = "Oh Sh*t": Gladiator II's Paul Mescal Reveals How He Reacted To The Maximus Twist | first = Adam | last = Bentz }}</ref>

On the first day of the [[2024 NFL season]], Paramount Pictures and [[Pepsi]] announced a campaign cross-promoting the film with the soft drink's sponsorship of the [[National Football League]]. A series of advertisements featured football stars [[Josh Allen]], [[Derrick Henry]], [[Justin Jefferson]], and [[Travis Kelce]] as "Gridiron Gladiators", with [[Megan Thee Stallion]] appearing as Empress Megan.<ref>{{cite press release |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=PEPSI® KICKS OFF 2024 NFL SEASON WITH COLOSSAL CAMPAIGN INSPIRED BY PARAMOUNT PICTURES' UPCOMING "GLADIATOR II", STARRING MEGAN THEE STALLION AND NFL SUPERSTARS JOSH ALLEN, DERRICK HENRY, JUSTIN JEFFERSON, AND TRAVIS KELCE |url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/pepsi-kicks-off-2024-nfl-season-with-colossal-campaign-inspired-by-paramount-pictures-upcoming-gladiator-ii-starring-megan-thee-stallion-and-nfl-superstars-josh-allen-derrick-henry-justin-jefferson-and-travis-kelce-302238558.html |location=[[Purchase, New York]] |publisher=[[PepsiCo]] |agency=PR Newswire |date=September 5, 2024 |access-date=September 5, 2024}}</ref>

On October 4, 2024, Japanese [[professional wrestling]] promotion [[New Japan Pro-Wrestling]] announced that the movie would sponsor that year's [[King of Pro-Wrestling (2024)|King of Pro-Wrestling]] event on October 14, which is slated to be the first since 2019.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Thompson |first1=Andrew |title=Gladiator II movie starring Denzel Washington named main sponsor of NJPW King of Pro-Wrestling |url=https://www.postwrestling.com/2024/10/04/gladiator-ii-movie-starring-denzel-washington-named-main-sponsor-of-njpw-king-of-pro-wrestling/ |access-date=October 4, 2024 |work=POST Wrestling |date=October 4, 2024 |archive-date=October 4, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241004110339/https://www.postwrestling.com/2024/10/04/gladiator-ii-movie-starring-denzel-washington-named-main-sponsor-of-njpw-king-of-pro-wrestling/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On November 1, 2024, at [[Lucca Comics & Games]] 2024, to promote the film in Italian cinemas, [[Francesco Totti]] played a [[Roman centurion]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Il Gladiatore II e Francesco Totti sorprendono il Lucca Comics & Games |url=https://boxofficebiz.it/news/il-gladiatore-ii-e-francesco-totti-sorprendono-il-lucca-comics-games/ |access-date=November 2, 2024 |agency=boxofficebiz.it |publisher=boxofficebiz.it |date=November 1, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Francesco Totti gladiatore al Lucca Comics: sorpresa in piazza San Michele |url=https://www.lanazione.it/lucca/comics/francesco-totti-mybj6kn5 |access-date=November 2, 2024 |agency=lanazione.it |publisher=lanazione.it |date=November 1, 2024}}</ref> On November 11, 2024, [[Scuderia Ferrari]] drivers [[Charles Leclerc]] and [[Carlos Sainz Jr.]] attended the film's premiere in London as part of a collaboration with Paramount to promote the film, with the film's actors Paul Mescal, Connie Nielsen, and Fred Hechinger joining the team at the [[2024 Las Vegas Grand Prix]]. The film's logo appeared on Ferrari's car for the Grand Prix itself.<ref>{{cite news | date = November 11, 2024 | url = https://www.ferrari.com/en-EN/formula1/articles/scuderia-ferrari-hp-celebrates-together-with-paramount-the-release-of-gladiator-ii | access-date = November 18, 2024 | work = [[Scuderia Ferrari]] | title = Scuderia Ferrari HP celebrates together with Paramount the release of ''Gladiator II'' }}</ref> The London premiere was the first [[Royal Film Performance]] during the reign of [[Charles III]].

==Reception==
===Box office===
''Gladiator II'' grossed {{USD|172.4 million|long=no}} in the United States and Canada, and {{USD|289.7 million|long=no}} in other countries, for a worldwide total of {{USD|462.2 million|long=no}}.<ref name="NUM">{{cite web |title=Gladiator II (2024) - Financial Information |url=https://www.the-numbers.com/movie/Gladiator-II-(2024)#tab=box-office |website=[[The Numbers (website)|The Numbers]] |access-date=February 9, 2025 |archive-date=November 15, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241115021721/https://www.the-numbers.com/movie/Gladiator-II-(2024)#tab=box-office |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="BOM" />

In the United States and Canada, ''Gladiator II'' was projected to gross {{USD|60 million|long=no}} from 3,500 theaters in its opening weekend. It was released alongside ''[[Wicked (2024 film)|Wicked]]'', which was compared to 2023's [[Barbenheimer]] due to the films' contrasting target audiences.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2024/11/wicked-gladiator-box-office-preview-1236181463/|title='Wicked' To Win Over The World With $165M-$200M Opening; 'Gladiator II' Passing $100M Overseas Today With An Eye On $60M+ U.S. Weekend – Box Office Preview|date=November 19, 2024|first=Anthony|last=D'Alessandro|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|access-date=November 19, 2024|archive-date=November 20, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241120022203/https://deadline.com/2024/11/wicked-gladiator-box-office-preview-1236181463/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.boxofficepro.com/long-range-forecast-gladiator-ii-goes-to-battle-at-the-box-office/|title=Long Range Forecast: ''Gladiator II'' Goes to Battle at the Box Office|date=October 24, 2024|website=[[Boxoffice Pro]]|access-date=November 11, 2024}}</ref> The film made {{USD|22 million|long=no}} on its first day, including {{USD|6.5 million|long=no}} from Thursday night previews. It went on to debut to {{USD|55.5 million|long=no}}, finishing second behind ''Wicked''. It marked the biggest opening weekend of Denzel Washington's career, surpassing ''[[American Gangster (film)|American Gangster]]'' ({{USD|43.5 million|long=no}} in 2007), and also topped ''[[8 Mile (film)|8 Mile]]'' ({{USD|51.2 million|long=no}} in 2002) for the best opening for a November R-rated film.<ref name=opening>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2024/11/box-office-wicked-gladiator-ii-1236184897/|title='Wicked' & 'Gladiator II' AKA 'Glicked' Fuel $205M Combined Weekend, Best Pre-Thanksgiving Frame In 11 Years — Sunday AM Box Office Update|date=November 24, 2024|first=Anthony|last=D'Alessandro|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|access-date=November 24, 2024|archive-date=November 23, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241123235153/https://deadline.com/2024/11/box-office-wicked-gladiator-ii-1236184897/|url-status=live}}</ref> In its second weekend the film made {{USD|30.7 million|long=no}} (and a total of {{USD|44 million|long=no}} over the five day [[Thanksgiving (United States)|Thanksgiving frame]]), dropping 44% and finishing third behind ''[[Moana 2]]'' and ''Wicked''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2024/11/box-office-moana-2-wicked-thanksgiving-1236189131/|title= Chee Hoo Mania At The Box Office: 'Moana 2' $221M 5-Day Opening Is Best 5-Day & Thanksgiving Ever; 'Wicked' Wows $117M+ & 'Gladiator II' $44M – Sunday Update |date=December 1, 2024|first=Anthony|last=D'Alessandro|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|access-date=December 1, 2024}}</ref> In its third weekend the film made $12.5 million, remaining in third place.<ref>{{Cite web |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony |date=December 8, 2024 |title='Moana 2', 'Wicked' & 'Gladiator II' Driving Record Post-Thanksgiving Frame Near $132M – Sunday AM Update |url=https://deadline.com/2024/12/box-office-moana-2-wicked-pushpa-2-1236196509/ |website=Deadline Hollywood |language=en-US |access-date=December 8, 2024 |archive-date=December 7, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241207214609/https://deadline.com/2024/12/box-office-moana-2-wicked-pushpa-2-1236196509/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2024/film/news/box-office-moana-2-wins-weekend-a24s-y2k-craters-1236242608/|title=Box Office: 'Moana 2' Scores $52 Million in Second Weekend, A24's 'Y2K' Craters With $2 Million Debut|author=Rebecca Rubin|work=Variety|date=December 8, 2024|access-date=December 8, 2024|archive-date=December 8, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241208174755/https://variety.com/2024/film/news/box-office-moana-2-wins-weekend-a24s-y2k-craters-1236242608/|url-status=live}}</ref>

The film was released in 63 territories one week ahead of its U.S. release and earned {{USD|87 million|long=no}}, the biggest opening weekend of Scott's career.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2024/nov/18/gladiator-ii-takes-87m-to-break-ridley-scott-opening-box-office-record|title=Gladiator II takes $87m to break Ridley Scott opening box-office record|date= November 18, 2024|first=Catherine|last=Shoard|website=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=November 19, 2024}}</ref> The second weekend had ''Gladiator II'' earning {{USD|106 million|long=no}} worldwide to finish second behind ''Wicked'', with its {{USD|50.5 million|long=no}} internationally being slightly higher than the {{USD|50.2 million|long=no}} of its competitor.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2024/11/wicked-global-box-office-opening-gladiator-2-international-box-office-1236186177/|title='Wicked' Casts $164M+ Spell In Global Opening; 'Gladiator II' Thunders To $221M WW After 2nd Offshore Frame – International Box Office|publisher=Deadline|last=Tartaglione|first=Nancy|date=November 24, 2024|access-date=December 1, 2024|archive-date=December 1, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241201191618/https://deadline.com/2024/11/wicked-global-box-office-opening-gladiator-2-international-box-office-1236186177/|url-status=live}}</ref>

In late 2026, [[Matthew Belloni]] from ''[[Puck News]]'' reported the rumor that Scott "blamed Mescal for the film's underperformance due to not being "masculine enough" in the title role", hence why he replaced Mescal with [[Jacob Elordi]] as Hig in ''[[The Dog Stars (film)|The Dog Stars]]'' (2026). <ref>{{Cite web |last=Vejvoda |first=Jim |title=Ridley Scott Reportedly Says Paul Mescal Wasn't ‘Masculine Enough’ for Gladiator 2 |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/ridley-scott-reportedly-says-paul-mescal-wasnt-masculine-enough-for-gladiator-2 |website=[[IGN]] |access-date=1 September 2026 |date=1 September 2026 |archive-date= |archive-url= |url-status=live }}</ref> However, representatives for Scott strongly denied the claims in a statement to [[Entertainment Weekly]], calling the rumors completely untrue and clarifying that Scott highly valued his collaboration with Mescal and was eager to work with him again. The spokesperson affirmed that Mescal's departure from [[The Dog Stars]] was strictly due to a scheduling conflict with his rehearsal commitments for [[Sam Mendes]]' forthcoming
[[The Beatles – A Four-Film Cinematic Event|four-part Beatles biopic series]], in which Mescal is set to portray [[Paul McCartney]]. <ref>{{Cite web |last=Russell |first=Shania |title=Ridley Scott’s rep addresses rumor he blames Paul Mescal for Gladiator II’s box office performance |url=https://ew.com/ridley-scott-rep-addresses-rumored-feud-paul-mescal-12075929#:~:text=A%20rep%20for%20Ridley,at%20the%20box%20office. |website=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |access-date=1 September 2026 |date=1 September 2026 |archive-date= |archive-url= |url-status=live }}</ref> 

===Critical response===
[[File:Denzel Washington in 2024.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Washington was singled out and praised by critics.]]

{{Rotten Tomatoes prose|70|6.6|406|Echoing its predecessor while upping the bloodsport and camp, ''Gladiator II'' is an action extravaganza that derives much of its strength and honor from Denzel Washington's scene-stealing performance.|ref=yes|access-date=January 24, 2026}}{{cbignore}} [[Metacritic]], which uses a [[Weighted arithmetic mean|weighted average]], assigned the film a score of 64 out of 100, based on 62 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.<ref name="Metacritic">{{cite web |title=''Gladiator II'' |url=https://www.metacritic.com/movie/gladiator-ii |website=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[Fandom (website)#Fandom, Inc.|Fandom, Inc.]] |access-date=December 11, 2024 |archive-url= |archive-date= |url-status=}}</ref>{{cbignore}} Audiences polled by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film an average grade of "B" on an A+ to F scale (down from the first film's A), while those surveyed by [[PostTrak]] gave it a 77% overall positive score, with 64% saying they would "definitely recommend" it.<ref name="opening" />

Christopher Campbell at Rotten Tomatoes summarized the reviews as having praised the action, performances, story, and visuals, and said some argued that "plot-wise it's actually too similar to its predecessor".<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 11, 2024 |author=Christopher Campbell |title=Gladiator II First Reviews: The Grand Spectacle of Action and Intrigue You're Hoping For |url=https://editorial.rottentomatoes.com/article/gladiator-ii-first-reviews-the-grand-spectacle-of-action-and-intrigue-youre-hoping-for/ |archive-date=November 12, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241112155445/https://editorial.rottentomatoes.com/article/gladiator-ii-first-reviews-the-grand-spectacle-of-action-and-intrigue-youre-hoping-for/ |url-status=live |access-date=January 12, 2025 }}</ref> Nick Hyman at Metacritic stated that "most critics also feel that the film lives in the shadow of the more emotional and ultimately superior original."<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 20, 2024 |author=Nick Hyman |title=Best Movies Directed by Ridley Scott, Ranked |url=https://www.metacritic.com/pictures/best-ridley-scott-movies/2/ |website=[[Metacritic]] |access-date=January 22, 2024 }}</ref> Early reactions from the film's first screening at Paramount Studios in Los Angeles on October 18, 2024, were positive. Critics praised Scott's direction, the set pieces, battle sequences and Mescal's and Washington's performances, mentioning that Scott and Washington could be nominated for the [[Academy Awards]], but a few felt the film lacked an "emotional punch" when compared to the original film.<ref name="THR1streact">{{cite news |last=Thomas |first=Carly |title=''Gladiator II'' First Reactions From Early Screening: "A Total Spectacle With a Pulsating Pace" |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/gladiator-2-first-reactions-screening-1236035517/ |access-date=October 19, 2024 |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=October 18, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Garner |first=Glenn |date=October 20, 2024 |title=''Gladiator II'' First Reactions Call Ridley Scott's Sequel "Unhinged," "Deliciously Cinematic And Machiavellian": "Can't Believe Ridley Pulled This Off" |url=https://deadline.com/2024/10/gladiator-ii-first-reactions-ridley-scott-sequel-unhinged-deliciously-cinematic-machiavellian-1236121555/ |access-date=October 21, 2024 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Gladiator II First Reactions: Ridley Scott Has Done It Again |url=https://editorial.rottentomatoes.com/article/gladiator-ii-first-reactions-ridley-scott-has-done-it-again/ |website=Rotten Tomatoes |access-date=October 22, 2024 |language=en-US}}</ref> Film critic Scott Menzel deemed the film Scott's best since ''[[The Martian (film)|The Martian]]'' (2015), a "big, bloody and bad ass action spectacle" that builds upon the original film's legacy.<ref name="THR1streact" />

Filmmakers [[Christopher Nolan]] and [[Hannah Fidell]] named it among their favorite films of 2024.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://variety.com/lists/christopher-nolan-gladiator-2-michael-mann-barry-jenkins/the-fire-inside-2/ | title=Directors Pick Favorite Films of 2024: Christopher Nolan Praises 'Gladiator II,' Barry Jenkins on 'Nickel Boys,' Jeff Nichols on 'Sing Sing' and More | date=December 18, 2024 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=O'Flat |first1=Chris |title=65 Directors Pick Their Favorite Films of 2024 |url=https://www.indiewire.com/gallery/directors-pick-best-films-2024/ |access-date=December 30, 2024 |work=IndieWire |date=December 30, 2024 |archive-date=December 30, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241230231638/https://www.indiewire.com/gallery/directors-pick-best-films-2024/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Peter Gillibrand and Naomi Clarke of the [[BBC]] recount that Russell Crowe "criticised the creators of the Gladiator sequel for not understanding 'what made the first one special'[; Crowe said that] there was a 'daily fight ... to keep that moral core of the character' when ... filming the original. 'The amount of times they suggested sex scenes ... for Maximus – it's like "you're taking away his power",' he said. He also questioned the idea that Maximus had a relationship with ... Lucilla, describing it as 'crazy.' Russell also revealed people had come up to him in restaurants in Europe to complain after the sequel came out, to which he would say: 'It wasn't me, I didn't do it'."<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c9w7v5ej0gvo | title=Russell Crowe says Gladiator II creators misunderstood what made original 'special' | date=December 10, 2025 }}</ref>

===Historical inaccuracy===
Some inaccuracies include the siege of a [[Numidia]]n city by Roman [[trireme]]s<ref name="Laurence"/> and the presence of [[shark]]s in a [[naumachia]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= Peitzman |first=Louis|date=November 21, 2024 |title=Ask a Roman-History Professor: Were There Ever Sharks in the Colosseum? |url=https://www.vulture.com/article/ask-a-roman-history-professor-were-there-ever-sharks-in-the-colosseum.html |access-date=April 9, 2025 |website=Vulture.com |language=en-US}}</ref> Numidia had already been part of the Roman Empire for about 250 years during the reign of Caracalla.<ref>{{cite news |title=The Only History 'Gladiator II' Cares About Is Its Own |url=https://www.indiewire.com/features/general/gladiator-2-real-roman-history-1235068039/ |work=[[IndieWire]] |date=November 22, 2024 |access-date=November 22, 2024 |archive-date=November 22, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241122230812/https://www.indiewire.com/features/general/gladiator-2-real-roman-history-1235068039/ |url-status=live }}</ref> University of Chicago historian [[Shadi Bartsch]] described the film as "total Hollywood bullshit".<ref>{{cite news |title=The Real History Behind Ridley Scott's 'Gladiator II' and Life as a Fighter in the Ancient Roman Arena |url=https://www.smithsonianmag.com/history/the-real-history-behind-ridley-scotts-gladiator-ii-and-life-as-a-fighter-in-the-ancient-roman-arena-180985494/ |work=[[Smithsonian (magazine)|Smithsonian]] |date=November 21, 2024}}</ref> At the same time, baboons and a rhinoceros showcased on the Colosseum's arena are historically attested,<ref name="Laurence">{{cite web|url=https://lighthouse.mq.edu.au/article/november-2024/gladiator-2-how-historically-accurate-is-it|title=Gladiator II: How historically accurate is it?|author=[[Ray Laurence]]|publisher=[[Macquarie University]]|date=November 14, 2024|access-date=November 17, 2024|archive-date=November 21, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241121025329/https://lighthouse.mq.edu.au/article/november-2024/gladiator-2-how-historically-accurate-is-it|url-status=live}}</ref> although there is no record of gladiators riding a rhinoceros.<ref name="BBC History Magazine"/>

There could be no naval battles in the Colosseum during the time of Caracalla since the underground structures were equipped for staging traditional gladiatorial fights and wild animals hunting games. The complex housed machinery such as winches and lifts and as a result naval games would have been impossible. Scholar [[Ray Laurence]] noted that "the ancient admiration of those who defy death as gladiators is nicely set out by the film" and that "the culture of gladiators is well presented with a doctor of gladiators".<ref name="Laurence" /><ref name="BBC History">{{cite news |first=Jonny |last=Wilkes |title=The real Macrinus: how Gladiator II's power broker became a short-lived Roman emperor |url=https://www.historyextra.com/period/roman/macrinus-real-roman-emperor/ |work=BBC History Magazine |date=November 15, 2024 |access-date=November 22, 2024 |archive-date=November 17, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241117143620/https://www.historyextra.com/period/roman/macrinus-real-roman-emperor/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Screen Rant">{{cite news |title=Gladiator 2's Denzel Washington Reflects On Historical Inaccuracy Of His Character: "Macrinus Wasn't Black" |url=https://screenrant.com/gladiator-2-macrinus-historical-inaccuracy-denzel-washington-response/ |work=[[Screen Rant]] |date=November 22, 2024 |access-date=November 22, 2024 |archive-date=November 22, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241122220805/https://screenrant.com/gladiator-2-macrinus-historical-inaccuracy-denzel-washington-response/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

The casting of [[Denzel Washington]] as [[Macrinus]] generated discussion regarding historical accuracy. The historical Macrinus was born into an [[equestrian class]] [[Berbers|Berber]] family in [[Mauretania Caesariensis]], North Africa, and historical records indicate he was a [[praetorian prefect]] who dealt with military and legal affairs, rather than a former gladiator owner as depicted in the film.<ref>{{cite news |title=Which Characters from Gladiator II Are Real? |url=https://www.biography.com/history-culture/a62977525/are-characters-from-gladiator-ii-real |work=Biography.com |date=November 21, 2024 |access-date=November 22, 2024 |archive-date=November 22, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241122215232/https://www.biography.com/history-culture/a62977525/are-characters-from-gladiator-ii-real |url-status=live }}</ref> The depiction led to criticism in [[North Africa]], particularly among commentators and audiences in [[Algeria]], who accused the production of "blackwashing" and argued that portraying the Berber emperor as a Black sub-Saharan African inaccurately erased North African identity.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Solante |first=Amira |date=November 19, 2024 |title=Gladiator 2 relance la polémique sur l'histoire et la couleur |url=https://www.lexpressiondz.com/chroniques/l-ecran-libre/gladiator-2-relance-la-polemique-sur-l-histoire-et-la-couleur-329221 |website=L'Expression (Algérie) |access-date=November 26, 2024 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lyes |first=Sonia |date=October 26, 2024 |title=Gladiator 2 : Polémique en Algérie autour de Macrinus, l'empereur berbère de Rome |url=https://www.tsa-algerie.com/gladiator-2-polemique-en-algerie-autour-de-macrinus-lempereur-berbere-de-rome/ |website=Tout sur l'Algérie |access-date=November 26, 2024}}</ref> In response, Washington acknowledged that the historical Macrinus was not Black, but noted the historical presence of various African and diverse populations within the Roman Empire during that era.<ref>{{cite web | date=November 22, 2024 |author=Jonathan Dean | url=https://www.thetimes.com/culture/film/article/denzel-washington-gladiator-ii-interview-ls9dv88qw | title=Denzel Washington: 'I made some real clunkers after Malcolm X' | website=[[The Times]] |url-access=limited |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241118022711/https://www.thetimes.com/culture/film/article/denzel-washington-gladiator-ii-interview-ls9dv88qw |archive-date=November 18, 2024 | access-date=December 30, 2024}}</ref><ref name="Screen Rant"/> The film also attracted attention for Washington's [[New York accent]], with some social media reactions criticizing the perceived historical inauthenticity and use of modern [[American accent|American speech]] patterns in a film set in ancient Rome.<ref name=Bond>{{cite web |last=Bond |first=Sarah |title=Why Do We Expect Ancient Romans to Have British Accents in Movies? |url=https://hyperallergic.com/why-do-we-expect-romans-to-have-british-accents-in-movies/ |website=[[Hyperallergic]] |date=August 12, 2024 |access-date=May 11, 2026}}</ref> Jermaine Bryant, a Roman historian and PhD candidate in Classics at [[Princeton University]], suggested that the filmmakers’ decision to give Washington's character a New York accent could reflect a willingness by Hollywood to challenge the longstanding [[Queen's Latin|trope of portraying Romans with British accents]] and the broader British coding traditionally associated with Roman characters.<ref name=Bond/>

The emperors Caracalla and Geta were not twins{{mdash}}Caracalla was about one year older than Geta. They became the joint emperors in 211 on the death of their father, [[Lucius Septimius Severus]] (emperor from 193 to 211).  They hated each other and barely spoke with each other from at least the time of their father's death.  The two were not at all on friendly terms as depicted in the film.  Within a year of their becoming co-emperors, Caracalla murdered Geta.  Macrinus was not involved in this.

Caracalla went on as emperor until 217 when he was murdered in Syria by one Justin Martialis, a disgruntled soldier, possibly in a conspiracy arranged by Macrinus.
Shortly afterwards Macrinus declared himself emperor and his young son [[Diadumenianus]] (who is not depicted in the film) a co-emperor. Both Macrinus and his son were killed in Asia Minor (not in the outskirts of Rome as in the film) in 218 in their struggle to stay in power against the challenge from [[Elagabalus]], a Syrian-born high-priest of a local Syrian sun god of the same name, who then became emperor.<ref>{{cite book |title=The Decline and the Fall of the Roman Empire, Book 1, Chapter VI |url=https://www.gutenberg.org/files/731/731-h/731-h.htm#chap06.1 |author=Edward Gibbon |date=1776 |access-date=January 28, 2026}}</ref>  The film depicts Macrinus as being killed by the young Lucius Verus, the son of [[Lucilla]], daughter of Marcus Aurelius.  But this is not possible.  The real-life Lucilla was the wife of [[Lucius Verus]], co-emperor with Marcus Aurelius, his adoptive brother.<ref>{{cite book |title=The Decline and the Fall of the Roman Empire, Book 1, Chapter IV |url=https://www.gutenberg.org/files/731/731-h/731-h.htm#chap04.1 |author=Edward Gibbon |date=1776 |access-date=January 28, 2026}}</ref>  She was born in 148 or 150, so by the time Severus died, she would have been 61 or 63 years old, much older than she is depicted in the film.  One of her sons with Lucius Verus was also named Lucius Verus, as in the film. Lucilla had actually died some 20 years before the reign of Caracalla, being murdered on the orders of her brother, the then Emperor Commodus; her son Lucius had died in childhood.<ref name="BBC History Magazine">{{cite news |first=Kev |last=Lochun |title=Sharks in the arena? Gladiator II's real history and historical accuracy explained |url=https://www.historyextra.com/period/roman/gladiator-ii-real-history-true-story/ |work=BBC History Magazine |date=November 15, 2024 |access-date=November 22, 2024 |archive-date=November 22, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241122132737/https://www.historyextra.com/period/roman/gladiator-ii-real-history-true-story/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=The Real Roman History Behind 'Gladiator II', Explained |url=https://www.esquire.com/uk/culture/a61499972/roman-history-behind-gladiator-ii-true-story/ |work=Esquire |date=July 9, 2024 |access-date=November 24, 2024 |archive-date=August 28, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240828191706/https://www.esquire.com/uk/culture/a61499972/roman-history-behind-gladiator-ii-true-story/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Caracalla, after becoming sole emperor, naming his pet as consul was possibly inspired by the earlier Roman emperor [[Caligula]], who according to [[Suetonius]] intended to name his horse [[Incitatus]] as consul.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cava |first=Marco della |title=Fact-checking 'Gladiator II': Were there really sharks in the Colosseum? |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/entertainment/movies/2024/11/23/gladiator-2-true-story-fact-check/76387624007/ |access-date=November 30, 2024 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US |archive-date=November 26, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241126232742/https://www.usatoday.com/story/entertainment/movies/2024/11/23/gladiator-2-true-story-fact-check/76387624007/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

An idea that is presented in both ''Gladiator'' films is the [[Branding iron|branding]] of gladiators. This myth comes from an incorrect interpretation of the ''[[Sacramentum (oath)|sacramentum]]'' of gladiators, which when translated into English means "I swear to let myself be burned" (bonded, punished, and killed with fire). The way this should be interpreted is more of a reference to combat than an actual mark that would identify you as a gladiator. However, this practice of marking did happen but only to [[slavery|slaves]] attempting to escape from their masters. Slaves running away from their masters were considered robbers because Romans believed when a slave tried running away from his master, he was "stealing himself" from his owner, so they would mark him so people would know he is a slave if he tried to run away again.<ref>{{Cite web |last=World |first=SPQR {{!}} Ancient Rome and the Ancient |date=January 30, 2024 |title=Common Misconceptions about Gladiators |url=https://medium.com/@ancient.rome/common-misconceptions-about-gladiators-1498cf69af52 |access-date=December 1, 2024 |website=Medium |language=en}}</ref>

There is no historical record of a Roman general named Acacius.<ref name="BBC History Magazine"/> The Roman co-emperors Caracalla and Geta were of mixed [[Arab]], [[Roman Italy|Italic]], [[Ancient Libya|Libyan]] and [[Punic]] descent, but the actors who played them are not.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Birley |first=Anthony R. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=z8iEAgAAQBAJ&dq=Septimius+Severus+libyan+by+race&pg=PA50 |title=Septimius Severus: The African Emperor |date=June 1, 2002 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-134-70745-4 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Hollywood's Gladiator II: Another missed opportunity for authentic North African representation |url=https://www.newarab.com/features/gladiator-ii-missed-chance-north-african-representation |work=[[The New Arab]] |date=August 9, 2024 |access-date=November 22, 2024 |archive-date=September 21, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240921183103/https://www.newarab.com/features/gladiator-ii-missed-chance-north-african-representation |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Sequel==
In September 2024, Scott said that he was developing a script for a third film, but that it would depend on the reception for the second installment. Titled ''Gladiator III'', the plot was stated to follow the continuing adventures of Lucius Verus. Likening the ending of ''Gladiator II'' to ''[[The Godfather Part II]]'' (1974), the filmmaker stated that the next movie would explore the character's realization that he was now tasked with a continuing reputation that he does not want.<ref name="Future_Premiere">{{cite web |url=https://www.premiere.fr/Cinema/News-Cinema/Ridley-Scott-prepare-deja-Gladiator-3--exclu|work=Premiere|title=Ridley Scott is already preparing Gladiator 3 [exclusive]|author=Picard, Sylvestre|date=September 20, 2024|access-date=September 20, 2024}}</ref><ref name="Future_Variety">{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2024/film/news/ridley-scott-gladiator-3-ideas-development-1236151985/|work=Variety|title=Ridley Scott Is 'Already Toying With the Idea' for 'Gladiator 3': 'Seriously! I've Lit the Fuse'|author=Sharf, Zack|date=September 20, 2024|access-date=September 24, 2024|archive-date=September 23, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240923213751/https://variety.com/2024/film/news/ridley-scott-gladiator-3-ideas-development-1236151985/|url-status=live}}</ref> Scott later stated that the movie is in early stages of development and intended to be the next project he works on,<ref name="Future_THR">{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/gladiator-iii-ridley-scott-1236008160/|work=The Hollywood Reporter|title=Ridley Scott Planning a 'Gladiator 3': "There's Already an Idea"|author=Hibberd, James & Aaron Couch|date=September 20, 2024|access-date=September 24, 2024}}</ref> though the following month he told ''[[The New York Times]]'' his next projects after ''Gladiator II'' would be a [[Bee Gees]] biopic, set to shoot in September 2025, and an adaptation of the [[science fiction]] novel ''[[The Dog Stars]]'', set to shoot in Italy in April 2025.<ref name="TNYT Scott" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Sir Ridley Scott on Gladiator II |url=https://podcasts.apple.com/ca/podcast/sir-ridley-scott-on-gladiator-ii/id1616559297?i=1000676935493 |access-date=November 24, 2024 |website=Apple Podcasts |language=en-CA |archive-date=November 21, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241121044652/https://podcasts.apple.com/ca/podcast/sir-ridley-scott-on-gladiator-ii/id1616559297?i=1000676935493 |url-status=live }}</ref> In August 2025, Scott revealed that the film "is in process right now".<ref>{{Cite news |last=Pelley |first=Rich |date=August 28, 2025 |title=‘I turned down $20m to do Terminator 3. I can’t be bought, dude’: Ridley Scott on directing, Daleks and ... cherry jam |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2025/aug/28/i-turned-down-20m-to-do-terminator-3-i-cant-be-bought-dude-ridley-scott-on-directing-daleks-and-cherry-jam |access-date=March 21, 2026 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>
